text:
After co-inventing ChatGPT, I kept asking myself: why have superhuman chat models not led to AGI?

I’ve spent the last 2 years in stealth building a new way to train models (RLCD), and a new type of frontier AI model that we are releasing today: Jev

• 20-200x faster
• 40-400x cheaper (w/ output tokens free)
• Frontier composable intelligence optimized for decisions

AFAICT the shortest path to AI-based economic revolution

今天送一位上周被 layoff的老朋友去机场，ta决定回国发展了，我们聊了很多，也都认为我们的职业可能会在 5 年左右消失。

难以想象一年半之前，我们还在对话框里跟 AI 聊天，把代码复制进去，再复制出来。写代码还是 Tab Tab Tab，用 Copilot 补全，而不是让 AI 直接写

我们也聊到了硅谷湾区这个反人类的地方，如果你是顶级天才，或者有不得不的理由在这里打工谋生、追求人生进步，这确实是个绝佳的地方，但它也是大多数人的围城

如果你随意找在这里的 10 个中国人，我想至少有5个都会跟你说，这里很无聊，想离开这里。这里的人种多样性堪比中关村创业大街

硅谷的确是一个会让人变土、变单调，变得人生方向收窄的地方。

回来的路上我在想，如果我没有从事计算机，在纽约、洛杉矶、上海，我的人生会不同吗？

我前男友一晚上八次，差点把我操疯了。我分手了阿，受不了，就是因为受不了才分手，我逼不耐磨。主要是他时间也很久啊，差不多二十分钟，我觉得我两次就有点难忍了。一下子下午到第二天下午八次，吓得我回家了。

​全是痛啊，根本没有技巧。刚开始可能还有点感觉吧，后来就是想哭。我前男友16cm，不是很粗，但是很长，他后入会顶的我里面很痛很痛，正常的姿势还能好一点，然后后入的时候速度又特快。我会一直往前爬，然后他就把我抓回去。后来我绕着桌子跑，他就一直想绕着桌子抓我操我。我觉得太恐怖了，他根本就不尊重我的意愿，我都说了我很痛，他非要操我。

​我俩就见了一次，刚开始是在酒店见的。然后他问我是不是饿了，说我先给你点个外卖垫点。我当时还觉得他人挺好的，就是特别在意我的情绪、特别考虑我。结果吃完饭之后就开始抱着我说痒了，然后就一直操我。

​我们俩是下午见面的，晚上又点了个外卖，然后吃，吃完了之后就抱着我睡觉，还把我给操醒了。早晨起来也是点外卖。然后我上午说我想出去玩，让他带我出去玩，他跟我说“你还下得了床啊”，然后就继续操我。

​他妈的，一直到下午，我实在是受不了了，然后我就趁着他睡午觉出去了。分手三年多了，一直没有做过爱，我觉得我不会再谈恋爱了，我害怕被日的四仰八叉，太痛苦了，我已经有心理阴影了。我从此之后再也没谈过男朋友，我觉得太恐怖了，我操。

text:
Docker Hub 上的 minio/minio 正式 404，标志着这个十亿级开源神作的免费时代彻底画上句号。回顾 MinIO 这几年的商业化演变，堪称教科书级的“逐步劝退”三部曲：先是一刀切砍掉打磨多年的 Web 管理控制台；随后归档仓库、停止公开推送 CVE 安全补丁；如今彻底清空 Docker Hub 公共镜像，掐断最后的公共分发渠道，全面逼迫用户走向商业版 AIStor。

对于还在生产集群跑着旧镜像的团队而言，这已经不是“能不能凑合用”的问题，而是实打实的高危隐患：新节点扩容和 CI/CD 构建会因为镜像拉取失败直接挂死，缺失 CVE 补丁则让企业合规审计完全无法通过。

生产应急与替代路径：

短期止血：部署脚本可临时切换至未下架的 Quay 镜像源 救急；更稳妥的做法是立刻在现有存活节点执行 docker save 导出镜像，推送到内网私有 Harbor，切断对外部公共 Registry 的单点依赖。

社区分支：如果业务重度依赖既有配置与特性，可关注社区主导维护的 MinIO Fork 项目 pgsty/silo。

轻量替代：本地测试与小型边缘节点，推荐转投由 Rust 构建的 Garage 或 RustFS，资源占用低且部署极快。

架构重构：大规模分布式自建建议硬啃 SeaweedFS；若无专属运维团队，直接采购各厂商托管的 S3 或 Cloudflare R2，很多时候云账单远比承担安全与运维事故的隐形成本划算。

开源的尽头终究要面对商业现实，当外部白嫖红利见底，自建基础设施的断供风险与维护成本必须尽早计入技术债务。

#开源 #MinIO #DevOps #Docker

短期止血：部署脚本可临时切换至未下架的 Quay 镜像源 救急；更稳妥的做法是立刻在现有存活节点执行 docker save 导出镜像，推送到内网私有 Harbor，切断对外部公共 Registry 的单点依赖。

社区分支：如果业务重度依赖既有配置与特性，可关注社区主导维护的 MinIO Fork 项目 pgsty/silo。

轻量替代：本地测试与小型边缘节点，推荐转投由 Rust 构建的 Garage 或 RustFS，资源占用低且部署极快。

架构重构：大规模分布式自建建议硬啃 SeaweedFS；若无专属运维团队，直接采购各厂商托管的 S3 或 Cloudflare R2，很多时候云账单远比承担安全与运维事故的隐形成本划算。

开源的尽头终究要面对商业现实，当外部白嫖红利见底，自建基础设施的断供风险与维护成本必须尽早计入技术债务。

懵逼了，我之前每个月 200 刀给 OpenAI，感觉完全没把 Pro 的价值发挥出来，亏麻了😅😅😅

才发现，原来 Pro 还能这么用：

1、网页端连 GitHub 提 PR
把仓库连上 ChatGPT，让 Pro 当架构师，自己开分支改 UX、提 PR，构建失败再丢给本地修。

2、Codex 桌面端左上角开 Pro 对话
Codex 左上角能直接开 Pro，它带着你当前项目的完整上下文，深度分析完，点个加号就能直接把对话记录导给 Codex 继续干活。

3、把 Pro 当 MCP 接入 Codex
如果想让它更常驻，开源社区直接做好了现成的 MCP 桥（比如 codex-chatgpt-web），选 Zero Risk 模式，既能吃到网页端 Pro 的深度推演，又规避了封号风险。

之前真是亏麻了啊！！！

text:
兄弟们，AGI这波真的来了！！！万万没想到，这竟然是中国的模型，不是千问，不是豆包，而是最让人想不到的地方搞出来的，OpenAI和Anthropic没做成的卡点，他们全都实现了

自动化、技能调用、办公工作区、经济价值、网络安全、机器学习工程、深度研究、软件工程，Atria 已经能跟 GPT / Claude / DeepSeek / Kimi / Qwen / GLM 这一档正面硬刚了

我来说一下它到底强在哪：

AutomationBench 第一（53.8）
CyberGym 第一（86.5） 也就是「能自动干活」「网络安全场景」，模型是绝对不会出现逃逸的情况

真的赶紧试试！！！

quotedTweet.text:
兄弟们！科研人自媒体人的福音来了！！最近身边几个百万fo大佬都在用一个叫 Atria Dawn Preview的科研模型，我一开始以为它只和论文、实验室有关，没太关心

直到我让他从原始资料到完成正式报告，我才真的觉得他是有点东西的，而且，可以用科研的思维帮你完成生活中的任何一个任务

我给了@AtriaASI 12 份 SEC 申报文件、XBRL 公司数据和财务表，对比 NVIDIA、AMD、Intel 的研发与产能投入，判断三家公司的资本配置方式，最后交付一份 7 到 10 页的中文报告，要写一条“英伟达、AMD、Intel，谁更会把钱花在刀刃上”的行业深度内容交付给客户

模型接下来做的，刚好是最累最费时间的前半程，它先扫描工作区，把不同来源的文件找齐

再统一三家公司的财年和统计口径，读取表格、计算研发投入、资本开支和现金流，交叉核验重复数字

中间留下 15 次可观察的工具调用轨迹

最后生成图表、证据、反证和跟踪指标，落成一份 10 页中文 PDF。每个关键数字都要求能追溯到原始申报、工作表

普通聊天模型更擅长接着我的话往下写

这下我真知道科研Agent跟普通日常的Agent的区别在哪，科研 Agent 真的太适合用来搞自媒体了，它能够告诉你

哪些结论有原始来源
哪些数字重新计算过
哪些资料互相冲突
哪些地方现在还不能下判断
最后能不能交出一份真正可检查的文件

以后所有人用这类模型做内容，不会只丢一句“帮我写篇文章”

可以把选题、原始材料和交付标准一起给它，让它先把研究任务做完

文章的观点、故事和表达还是自己定

但最耗时间的资料阅读、数据核验、制图和研究底稿，可以先交给模型

学生写论文、产品经理做竞品、职场人写汇报、创作者做行业深度内容，其实都在处理同一种任务：

把一堆散乱材料，变成一个经得住追问的结果

Atria Dawn Preview来自上海人工智能实验室

官方 GitHub 已公开项目说明、模型地址和最终评测结果，代码与模型权重采用 MIT License

它现在还是 Preview 阶段，普通用户直接使用的门槛不算低

但“模型不只回答问题，而是读取材料、调用工具并交付文件”这条能力路线，已经很明确了

quotedTweet.text:
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Max) is a breakthrough in performance to cost efficiency. With +4.87% net improvement at $0.07 cost per median task, it’s reshaped the Pareto frontier for Agent Arena!

Among the top 3 open models, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Max) has the lowest median task cost. For comparison, it retains:
- 98% of Hy4 preview’s net improvement, at 73% lower cost
- 76% of Kimi K3 (Max)’s performance, at 92% lower cost.

Against models as powerful as Fable 5 or stronger, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Max) retains 35–54% of their net improvement at 97–99% lower cost. Those top models cost 37–76× more per task.

Net improvement over Arena baseline | Median cost/task:
- Claude Fable 5.1 (Max): +13.90% | $4.54
- GPT 6 Astra (Max): +11.90% | $4.09
- Claude Opus 5 (Max): +11.09% | $3.52
- Claude Opus 5 (High): +10.49% | $2.24
- Claude Fable 5 (High): +9.03% | $2.19
- Claude Opus 4.8 (High): +7.75% | $1.36
- GPT 5.6 Sol (xHigh): +7.40% | $1.09
- Kimi K3 (Max): +6.39% | $0.77
- Hy4 preview: +4.96% | $0.22
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Max): +4.87% | $0.06

With this release, GPT-5.6 Luna (xHigh), GLM-5.3-Flash, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash fell off the Pareto frontier for Agent Arena.

Congrats again to the @deepseek_ai team on this release!

text:
Passenger: Your Honor, this airline owes me $75,000 because they moved me to a different seat on my flight.

Airline Lawyer: That's not what happened. He was given another seat because of an operational issue.

Judge: You are suing an airline for $75,000 because they changed your seat?

Passenger: Yes, Your Honor.

Judge: What happened after they moved you?

Passenger: That's the part they don't want this court to hear.

Airline Lawyer: Your Honor, this is being exaggerated.

Judge: Then you shouldn't have a problem with me hearing it.

Passenger: I was originally sitting in 14A.

Judge: And where were you moved?

Passenger: 27C.

Judge: Why?

Passenger: The airline said they needed my original seat for another passenger.

Airline Lawyer: We offered him a better seat.

Passenger: It wasn't better.

Judge: What happened when you sat in 27C?

text:
妈的，今天三观真被狠狠干碎了一次。
跟朋友家的月嫂聊天。
阿姨一单 1.6 万，干了十几年，现在全部接私单，排期已经排到明年 6 月。

我当时已经觉得很猛了。

结果聊开心以后，她随口说了一句：

“我儿子也不出去上班，就在家赚钱。有时候一天能赚好几万。”

我第一反应：炒股？炒币？
阿姨说，不是。
直播。
唱歌、跳舞、聊天，靠打赏赚钱。
我当时脑子停了几秒。

一个妈妈，靠十几年口碑把自己的劳动力卖到 1.6 万一单，订单排到明年。
一个儿子，坐在家里把情绪价值卖给几千几万个人，一天流水几万。
一家两口，既没有融资，没有 AI，没有宏大叙事，也不天天研究什么商业模式、认知跃迁、财富自由

text:
I recently sat next to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on a flight from San Francisco to Frankfurt

After a few glasses of wine, he put his hand on my knee and whispered in my ear

“Wanna see something crazy?” he turned his laptop toward me

“These are our EU revenue projections and user numbers”

I gasped in shock

Exposing user data without consent is illegal in the EU and a massive GDPR violation

I excused myself and informed the flight attendant about this criminal misconduct 

When we landed, officers were already at the gate

They cuffed Sam on the jet bridge and took him to jail

In Europe, unlike in the US, the law applies to everyone

从事过水产相关工作的朋友和我说：

日本的水产怎么可能没有寄生虫，一样的有。只是他们也习惯有虫了，就要吃生的。

日本的血吸虫治疗技术，世界第一，无人望其项背。

究其原因，就是因为他们病例样本多。

text:
人很难写出自己真正没经历过的东西。

曹雪芹没参加过科举，但写贾府的富贵生活极细：虾丸鸡皮汤、酒酿清蒸鸭，吃什么、穿什么，布料材质、器物摆设，很多地方都细到可以拿来考据。

但写到贾政考宝玉功课，反而明显简单了。宝玉明明承载着贾府对科举的希望，实际写出来的考学方式居然大多只是对对子，也很少涉及名师指点、八股训练，更不用说破题、承题、引经据典这些具体细节。

高鹗恰好相反，农家子弟出身，正儿八经考取的功名。

他写贾府生活，能写出“黛玉爱吃五香大头菜”这种b话；可一写到科举，突然具体起来了：怎么破题，怎么引经据典，文章怎么起承转合，都写得很熟。

人确实很难写好自己根本没经历过的东西。

2016 年，应届生 Java 面试：
面试官：Java 有指针吗？
候选人：没有
面试官：你已经完全懂 Java 了，明天来上班。 

2026 年，应届生 Java 面试：
面试官：Java 有指针吗？
候选人：你想要的话，我可以用 Unsafe 给你手搓一个。
面试官：我不是这个意思…
候选人：哦，是想要智能指针吗，那得多给点时间
面试官：说了不是这个意思
候选人：哦哦哦懂你意思，unsafe 那堆操作在高版本 jdk 里都被标弃用了，嫌太脏了是吧，我用 JNI 写，或者你们版本高点？FFM也行的
面试官：……

这十年，到底发生了些什么啊

quotedTweet.text:
为什么“老头们”很难拒绝“精神小妹”

那天在网吧上网，旁边坐着一个精神小妹，看着也就十八九岁的样子，看我在玩英雄联盟，就主动跟我说 “哥，看你玩的不错，一起打两把啊”

我正好一个人也没啥意思 就一起玩了

还别说她这个操作还真可以，不比我差多少，

结果不到一个小时 她就说 她网费没了，哥你帮我冲10块我再陪你玩两把。

我一下就明白了，原来你这小妹在这等我呢？

我直接给她冲了二十还给她点了杯果汁，给她开心坏了，又陪我玩了好几个小时，后来她的小姐妹们给她打视频，找她去吃米线。

我一听 直接跟她说 正好我也饿了，今天玩的挺开心，你把她们叫过来，我请客，让你们吃点好的。

她这一听眼睛都亮了，她直接就在视频里把小姐们都叫来了。

我找了个档次一般的餐厅，甚至比我平时去的还要低点，六七个小姑娘 点了一桌子菜 才花了300多。

饭桌上她说 这是今天我在网吧认识的哥哥，人可好了 给我冲了网费还请我喝果汁，还要请咱们吃大餐。

结果小姐妹们一听 疯狂向我眨眼，说谢谢哥哥，还一个个主动过来加了我的微信。

周末，表弟给我介绍了一个相亲对象，34岁有点胖，但是只要30万的彩礼。 

我瞬间索然无味。。。

为什么“老头们”很难拒绝“精神小妹”

那天在网吧上网，旁边坐着一个精神小妹，看着也就十八九岁的样子，看我在玩英雄联盟，就主动跟我说 “哥，看你玩的不错，一起打两把啊”

我正好一个人也没啥意思 就一起玩了

还别说她这个操作还真可以，不比我差多少，

结果不到一个小时 她就说 她网费没了，哥你帮我冲10块我再陪你玩两把。

我一下就明白了，原来你这小妹在这等我呢？

我直接给她冲了二十还给她点了杯果汁，给她开心坏了，又陪我玩了好几个小时，后来她的小姐妹们给她打视频，找她去吃米线。

我一听 直接跟她说 正好我也饿了，今天玩的挺开心，你把她们叫过来，我请客，让你们吃点好的。

她这一听眼睛都亮了，她直接就在视频里把小姐们都叫来了。

我找了个档次一般的餐厅，甚至比我平时去的还要低点，六七个小姑娘 点了一桌子菜 才花了300多。

饭桌上她说 这是今天我在网吧认识的哥哥，人可好了 给我冲了网费还请我喝果汁，还要请咱们吃大餐。

TradingView yeni bir kapı açtı: Resmî MCP Server artık beta olarak kullanıma sunuldu.

Bunun anlamı şu: TradingView verileri ve bazı platform araçları artık ChatGPT, Claude ve MCP destekleyen diğer yapay zekâ istemcileriyle doğrudan bağlanabiliyor.

Şu anda MCP üzerinden OHLCV verileri, screener sonuçları, teknik göstergeler, haberler, temel veriler, ekonomik takvimler, watchlist’ler ve alert’ler gibi birçok veriye erişilebiliyor. Bazı işlemler, örneğin alert oluşturma ve watchlist yönetimi de destekleniyor.

Bağlantı OAuth 2.1 ile yapılıyor; API key gerekmiyor. TradingView tarafında özellik Essential ve üzeri planlarda sunuluyor.

Ben de bugün ChatGPT ile bağlantıyı kurup test etmeye başladım.

Şimdilik kişisel Pine Script indikatörlerinin kendi ürettiği özel değerleri doğrudan okumaya yönelik bir araç görünmüyor. Ancak MCP araç seti beta aşamasında ve TradingView bunun zamanla genişleyeceğini belirtiyor.

Bence asıl ilginç olan, piyasa verisi ile yapay zekâ arasındaki bu doğrudan bağlantının bundan sonra nereye evrileceği.

quotedTweet.text:
Codex 以任务为中心，Grok Bot 和 Muse 以 Bot 为中心，都是错误的产品范式。

它们看起来是两种不同的产品范式，但本质上犯了同一个错误：把 AI 的组织工作交给了用户。

Bot-centered 产品沿用了人类社会的组织方式：不同的人有不同的职业、角色和分工，于是 AI 也被拆成不同的 Bot、Expert、Agent。用户在开始工作之前，首先要判断：这件事应该找哪个 Bot？

Task-centered 产品则沿用了传统软件的信息组织方式：不同的事情属于不同的 Task、Chat、Project。于是用户又需要先创建一个 Task、开启一个 Chat、选择一个 Project，然后记住之后应该回到哪里继续这件事。

两种范式看似不同，本质上都要求用户分类。

这些产品的错误本质在于，把 AI 当作人，认为 AI 和人一样，要么要按职业、角色划分其功能性，用户使用 AI 时，也需要像在社会上招工一样，按照一定分工角色查找和使用 AI。

这些产品没有理解 AI 的本质 —— AI 不是人类，它是全知全能的「唯一神」，它不需要人类这一套社会分工。

用户不用关心这件事应该交给哪个 AI Bot，也不应该先判断它属于哪个 Chat、Task 或 Project。

用户只需要向“神”表达自己的意图。

“帮我看看昨天客户提到的问题。”
“把它整理成下周的产品计划。”
“顺便更新那个 presentation。”
“下周一提醒我跟进。”
“以后类似的客户反馈都自动放进去。”

对用户来说，这些应该发生在同一个持续存在的 AI relationship 中，而不是五个不同的 Bot、Task 或 Chat。

AI 作为「神」可以在后台理解：这是哪个 Intent，属于哪个 Episode，与哪个 Project、Task、Artifact、Object 有关，又应该写入什么 Memory、继承什么 Scope。

text:
memory has been a hot topic for the past ~2 years

every time we bring it up or do anything there, gets ton of interest, but nothing sticks

few takes on why below:

- how to update and then use memory needs to be pretty tightly integrated with the harness. so its hard to build a standalone memory product

- the hardest part of memory is the logic of deciding what to remember. storing and even querying memory is not necessarily hard. the logic of deciding what to remember is often (a) application specific, (b) just prompting, which makes it hard to productize

- memory is not that useful in a general purpose agent, but more for when you are doing repeated tasks. more high usage ai agent are not just doing the same task repeatedly

- memory hasnt really proven to be useful for coding agents, and most agent things that take off happen first in coding agents

text:
1997 年 WWDC，台下有个开发者当着全场人的面给乔布斯难堪：

“你很聪明，也很有影响力。但很遗憾，好几个关键问题上，你根本不知道自己在讲什么。”

全场瞬间死寂。
对方甚至当场补刀：你打算怎么用 Java 承接 OpenDoc？你过去这几年到底都在干什么？

乔布斯没有急着反唇相讥。
他低头沉默了很久，拧开水瓶慢慢喝了一口，才拿起话筒。

那段封神的 5 分钟回应里，有三点非常值得所有人学习：

1. 最难受的现实在于：当众挑战你的这帮人，在具体的局部细节上往往是对的。

2. 必须从用户体验倒推技术实现，绝不能拿着手里现成的锤子到处找钉子。

3. 这种错误他犯得比在座所有人都多，身上全是疤；苹果要活下去，很多哪怕再精巧的技术，也只能沦为断臂求生的代价。

很多人把这段封神现场当成以客户为中心的励志鸡汤，其实看浅了。

乔布斯赢的从来不是辩才，而是认知维度的降维打击：

他先大方承认对方在技术上完全合理，然后不动声色地把整场对话的战场换掉了：从乔布斯懂不懂技术细节，直接切换成苹果到底要砍掉什么才能活下去。

聚焦从来不是做加法，而是冷酷地做减法。敢对无数个局部正确的技术说不，才能收敛出一台能卖几十亿的成熟产品。

在众目睽睽下被当头泼冷水，还能不被情绪带偏、瞬间把议题拉回生死线，这才是顶级掌舵人的抗压底色。

在商业战场上，赢下技术争辩毫无意义。

最惨烈的死法，莫过于公司彻底破产了，而你手里的技术每一行都是对的。 https://t.co/WrfZ4VEpGk

text:
Today's inflation data, largely in-line with consensus expectations, but still well above the Fed's target, is a reminder rising prices will still be a major issue for investors & voters in this midterm election cycle. 🗳️

But what comes after the midterms is what long-term investors should try to stay focused on. Since 1938, the 12 months following a midterm has always generated positive returns for the S&P 500. It's less about who wins and more about lifting the cloud of uncertainty - the purple haze as I like to call it - that may be hanging over markets.

We expect the headline noise to get louder the closer we get to the election, so what's an investor do to?! Stay diversified and buckle up, because there's typically volatility heading into November. But soon enough it'll all be in the rearview mirror!

My latest @PNCBank Adding Alpha breaks it down.

text:
First Impressions of Opus 5.2

I've had access to the model for two days, and I have a lot to say about it

1. So far, it's the best model at understanding your intent. It builds chains of reasoning from indirect cues, and it does this with great taste and care

2. Very thorough. In terms of thoroughness it reminds me of GPT-5.6 Sol, but it doesn't get carried away with unnecessary tasks. It stays on course and takes into account every nuance you've described

3. The best handling of skills, MCP, and plugins I've seen. It's the first model that calls a plugin at the right moment. It doesn't burn tokens at the start of a request exploring its working environment the way every other model does. It can call an MCP or plugin closer to the end of its work, and it has a very good sense of how and where to apply them

4. Very diligent. I gave it a list of 8 huge tasks, and unlike Opus 5 or Fable 5.1, it never once stopped to ask unnecessary clarifying questions. It got everything to a working state and carefully verified its own results

5. Computer use and browser use have been massively improved. Based on first impressions, it's even better than Astra

6. It no longer does things it wasn't asked to do. In UI tasks, Opus 5 added a lot of its own ideas and sloppy design elements. Opus 5.2, on the other hand, respects the project's overall design code and UI components and doesn't reinvent the wheel

7. Finally, the first Claude model that writes in plain, clear language. I understand it the first time

8. Very token-efficient, even within a single session. It completed a huge pile of tasks and used only 60% of the session's context window. Fable 5.1 would have compacted its context three times with that amount of work

9. The best work with subagents. The model sees the big picture and knows when to spin up a subagent to parallelize a task and speed up execution. The best delegation skills so far. Fable 5.1 is much worse at this

10. During my work, I ran into a situation for the first time where Opus 5.2 was working as a subagent for Fable 5.1. The Opus subagent pushed back on the task Fable had assigned, asked for it to be corrected, pointed out all the mistakes, and only then took the task on. Just wow!

11. Intellectually, it's at least on par with Fable and Astra, and possibly even better

So far, I'm thrilled with this model. I haven't seen a single downside

text:
.@1Password's FLAWED report says AI models produce a clean security fix only 26% of the time.

Defenders shouldn't take that number seriously.                                                                                                                                        

• The six vulnerabilities were handpicked because their fixes were complex. Clean-fix rates ran from 3% to 60% depending on the bug, and the report averaged them together.

• Agents set up to fail were counted in the headline figure. Two of 1Password's prompts instructed the agent to apply the wrong fix. Those trials make up 22% of the data. One evaluation mode prevented the agent from compiling or running any code, and it accounts for 36% of the data.

• The report ran two models, GPT-5.5 at medium effort and Opus 4.8 at high. Neither was tested at its highest available setting, so the report says nothing about how more effort or stronger models change the results.

• Several instruction and grading errors further undercut the headline, and are elaborated upon in the attached blog.

We've spent four months submitting hundreds of AI-authored patches to widely adopted open-source projects as part of Patch the Planet.

Our experience didn't match 1Password's report, so we did a full analysis across 186 AI-authored pull requests and 33,500 subsequent commits, benchmarked against 2,265 human-authored patches we graded across years of security engagements. https://t.co/mdgED6y6eB

result.text:
.@1Password's FLAWED report says AI models produce a clean security fix only 26% of the time.

Defenders shouldn't take that number seriously.                                                                                                                                        

• The six vulnerabilities were handpicked because their fixes were complex. Clean-fix rates ran from 3% to 60% depending on the bug, and the report averaged them together.

• Agents set up to fail were counted in the headline figure. Two of 1Password's prompts instructed the agent to apply the wrong fix. Those trials make up 22% of the data. One evaluation mode prevented the agent from compiling or running any code, and it accounts for 36% of the data.

• The report ran two models, GPT-5.5 at medium effort and Opus 4.8 at high. Neither was tested at its highest available setting, so the report says nothing about how more effort or stronger models change the results.

• Several instruction and grading errors further undercut the headline, and are elaborated upon in the attached blog.

We've spent four months submitting hundreds of AI-authored patches to widely adopted open-source projects as part of Patch the Planet.

Our experience didn't match 1Password's report, so we did a full analysis across 186 AI-authored pull requests and 33,500 subsequent commits, benchmarked against 2,265 human-authored patches we graded across years of security engagements. https://t.co/mdgED6y6eB

text:
Stock market crash? 

AI is real. It will change industries, productivity, and probably the economy in ways we cannot fully see yet. 
  
But the market has been here before. In 1929, investors believed in a new economic era. 

In 2000, they were right that the internet would change everything. It did—but many investors still lost a lot of money because they paid too much for that future.    

Today, CAPE is again near the highest levels in history. 

It does not tell us the exact day a correction comes, but it has been very consistent about one thing: when valuations get this high, 5yrs and 10- year S&P 500 returns fall significantly.    

AI may be the future. That does not mean the current price of the future is reasonable.

If you are long the S&P500 dont expext long term returns to keep being so high.

Being a good stock picker will matter more and more.

text:
Mercor is committing $5M to a new AI Safety Fund.

One of the biggest challenges the industry faces today is addressing whether frontier AI is safe enough to deploy. This is why we believe investing today in safety research, evals, and verification is critical.

We want to work with AI researchers who are focused on critical safety risks, including:
 - Misalignment: deceptive alignment, reward hacking, scheming
 - Sandbox escape and agent containment failures
 - Evaluation awareness: models that behave differently when tested
 - Interpretability and scalable oversight
 - Red-teaming methodology and safety eval design

We will fund the researcher hours, API credits, and travel. We will also cover the cost to work with our network of 5M+ experts red-teaming, grading and annotation, and free use of our evals and analysis platform.

Grants are open to independent researchers, non-profits, and academics.

CLARITY may have stalled in the Senate today, but onchain capital markets still need to be built.

Liquidity is one of the biggest gaps, an issue that predates tokenization.

Semi-liquid funds hold more than $600 billion. Over $48 billion in redemption requests already exceeds available liquidity.

Tokenization upgrades custody, transfer, and settlement speed. It does not eliminate duration. A multi-year private credit loan does not become liquid just because the record moves onchain.

Mature capital markets solve this through intermediation: someone has to price the mismatch and stand between sellers and the asset’s natural liquidity cycle.

Introducing Fission, the liquidity layer for tokenized funds:
https://t.co/ddYFQFosDn

items.message: In the US Constitution, where does it say that the executive branch - which is a coequal branch - must abide by a supreme court opinion?

It doesn’t say that anywhere in the Constitution.

The document creates three separate branches and never states that the judiciary’s opinions bind the other two as a matter of constitutional command.

Relevant text:

- **Article III, Section 1** vests “the judicial Power of the United States” in “one supreme Court, and in such inferior Courts as the Congress may from time to time ordain and establish.” That is a grant of power to decide cases; it does not say the Court’s reasoning or future applications of that reasoning control the President.
- **Article II, Section 3** requires the President to “take Care that the Laws be faithfully executed.” The Constitution is the highest law, so this clause is the usual textual hook people use when arguing the President must follow court judgments. It does not mention the Supreme Court or its opinions.
- **Article VI** (Supremacy Clause) makes the Constitution, federal statutes, and treaties “the supreme Law of the Land” and binds *state judges*. It does not mention the President or treat Supreme Court opinions themselves as “supreme Law.”
- The presidential oath (Article II, Section 1) is to “preserve, protect and defend the Constitution,” not to preserve, protect and defend the Supreme Court’s interpretations of it.

The idea that the Court’s exposition of the Constitution is final and binding on the other branches comes from *Marbury v. Madison* (1803) and later cases such as *Cooper v. Aaron* (1958), not from the constitutional text. That is a judicially developed doctrine of judicial supremacy, not a clause you can point to.

A competing view (departmentalism) holds that each branch independently interprets the Constitution in the exercise of its own powers. Under that view the President must obey a final judgment directed at particular parties in a particular case, but is not constitutionally required to treat the Court’s broader reasoning as controlling in other contexts. The Constitution itself does not resolve the debate.

text:
Catalyzing Belief

the most underrated effect of AI and crypto is that they're producing a generation of believers

for decades, people have complained about visible stagnation in society. our parents' generation put a man on the moon while our best and brightest have focused on click-through rates and Snapchat filters

for all of human history, intelligence was scarce and transferring value required a gatekeeper. both constraints are breaking at once

fear around these industries is palpable. the push to regulate them will only accelerate because their potential for disruption is undeniable

for the first time in a long time, moonshots feel possible

people are dreaming about cures for cancer and Alzheimer's. tokenized stocks and borderless financial rails are showing early glimpses of a world where banking the unbanked is not a meme but a reality

when things are stagnant, every problem becomes zero-sum. when the pie isn't growing, you have no choice but to fight over crumbs

when all else fails, progress is the only answer. AI and crypto are the first catalysts in a generation that make people believe the pie can grow again

quotedTweet.text:
Can you, as a software engineer, whip out your phone, open some agent (Claude, Codex or whatever your company internally has) and ask it to do something that will involve 

- cloning repos 
- building/testing 
- raising PRs 
- accessing your JIRA/Notion/Linear 
- fetch required context from Slack 

At Meta for example this was technically possible. We can debate on effectiveness, efficiency, whether it was a good idea this was possible, and whether the number of people who worked on making this was a good investment of their time, but the point is it was possible. It is not a small investment. Do it poorly and soon you are spending $$$ more than LLMs in just spinning up VMs (RAM and SSD is costly!). These long running long paused sessions cannot remain always on VMs. Frequent pause-unpause of VM-like things in the cloud at 10s of thousands of employees scale is absolutely not trivial neither in cost, nor in orchestration.

Any company that has not achieved this state, but their CEO/CTO has glimpsed this reality, will not stop till they reach here. It is a supremely empowering state. It comes with the usual risks of 'execs vibing slop into our codebase' but that's part of the journey. 

Most companies are far from the ideal state in having good agentic infra setup properly.

$CIFR getting a major customer 1GW contract signed for Colchis BEFORE the December ERCOT audit could matter enormously.

Why?

A binding contract for the 1 GW Conditional Base Load would provide powerful evidence that:

• the load is real, not speculative
• there is an actual end-user for the power
• the project has commercial commitment
• financing and construction are more likely to proceed
• the requested 1 GW is genuinely needed

ERCOT still has to complete its audit and verification, so a contract doesn't guarantee final Base Load status.

But when regulators are deciding which massive new loads are sufficiently mature and credible to deserve scarce grid capacity, showing up with a hyperscaler contract is a very different proposition from showing up with an undeveloped 1 GW request.

Contract first → stronger audit case → greater confidence in favorable final power treatment.

That's why a Colchis 1GW customer announcement long before Dec is highly likely.

text:
To think Saudi Arabia has “no options” for the disruption on E-W is too simplistic. This is more of a product story. The Houthis were already targeting Saudi vessels in late July and Aug.

Yanbu loadings of products:
Aug 2026: ~350 KBPD 
Mar 2026 – Jul 2026 avg: ~ 500 KBPD

Yanbu loadings of oil:
Aug 2026: ~1.45 MBPD/ Sep 2026 MTD avg: ~1.8 MBPD (this is not even ONE VLCC per day that needs to be re-routed W->E to Ras Tanura to join the naval consort.)
Mar 2026 – Jul 2026 avg: ~3.85 MBPD

Now, refineries on the West Coast that depend on E-W pipeline for feedstock – Yasref , Samref, Yanbu with a combined capacity of > 1 MBPD are sol if the repairs take too long. Meaning, the ~ 350 KBPD of exports they were maintaining, mostly Gasoil, Diesel and Jet, headed for Europe are going to be constrained IF the disruption lasts months. There are some short term buffers however, as refiners maintain stocks. The terminal and refinery hub together has a capacity of ~ 35M BBLs, currently holding ~15 Million BBLs. If no loadings of oil happen at Yanbu, refiners may have a lifeline for approximately 2 weeks. So this isn't really a question of whether Saudi can reroute the products. It's whether Yanbu can maintain refinery output if crude feedstock from the east remains constrained.

I cannot tell you how long it will take to bypass the pumpstation at Masbah, that is for Aramco to tell us and I would not blindly trust sources that look at pictures and assume that the pump station itself must be fully repaired from the ground up to restore “some” flows. When it comes to engineering prowess in the field, very few can hold a candle to Aramco, IMO.

Btw, Ras Tanura loadings are picking up, and so are flows in the PG and GOO. 

Also, a reminder to everyone questioning people like Samir at TT, the difference between 8 MBPD and 12 MBPD is 2 VLCCs. Trying to find two dark VLCCs in that large a body of water is not an easy job, and don’t let people mislead you into thinking it is as easy as looking at a Sentinel-1 scene. It is not. It is the geographical equivalent of finding two needles in a very, very large haystack.

And before you @ me with “Houthis can do it again” (Houthis didn’t do this one, but, ok) and “But prices are soaring so you must be wrong.” This is an analysis of how things stand right now. And on price, there are two sides to the balance that fundamentally decides price; supply AND demand. People have a habit of picking whichever side suits their narrative and ignoring the other. Demand takes time to respond to price, and it will. Until then, the spot remains in deficit. SoH flows have recovered remarkably from the bottom, but total Middle East flows are still not fully normalized, while demand surged post MoU period.

This is going to be a good tweet to weed-out more of the riff-raff.

text:
Jesse Cancer Update #4:

Jesse's second bone marrow biopsy revealed that despite the intensive first 4 weeks of treatment & hospitalization (the "induction" phase), the Leukemia has persisted. He is, however, down to 1.5% cancer cells in his marrow - well improved from the 60% he had a diagnosis.  

Jesse is doubly rare. His is a T-cell ALL (accounting for only 20% of all Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia diagnosis, of which 80% are B-cell). To boot, his cancer is an early T cell precursor ALL (ETP-ALL) - which accounts for only 11% of ALL diagnoses. My child, he is special (just ask him). 🙂 

ETP-ALL is fairly nefarious and was once associated with historically poor outcomes. And the "residual disease" revealed by his most recent bone marrow biopsy at the end of induction is not what we wanted. Yet our excellent oncologists have accounted for the rarity of his sub-type and started him on a more aggressive protocol that they are confident will result in remission by his next bone marrow - around the end of October, God willing. If it does not, a bone marrow transplant will be considered. 

Please pray for Jesse's state of mind during this battle. Somewhere between a month of in-patient hospitalization, abrupt cessation of his phase 1 steroids, and initiation of the "consolidation" phase of treatment (chemo 5 days/week), Jesse developed steroid-induced psychosis. It was a side effect of his treatment that took us both by surprise. 

Please pray that his spirit is calmed, his mind is slowed, and that God shows Himself to be the very present help that we know He is. Pray God quiets my heart so that I may be laser-focused on Jesse's recovery and God's perfect faithfulness rather than on my own anxious thoughts that have a tendency -- even in the best of times -- to run unhelpfully amok.

God's mercies are sometimes severe. But they are mercies, nonetheless. And they are new every morning. Even in the Valley, He walks with us, sustaining us both in every moment, providing light for the path, strength for the day, hope for the moment.  

“For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways,” declares the Lord. “As the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways and my thoughts than your thoughts.” Isaiah 55: 8-9

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Max) is a breakthrough in performance to cost efficiency. With +4.87% net improvement at $0.07 cost per median task, it’s reshaped the Pareto frontier for Agent Arena!

Among the top 3 open models, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Max) has the lowest median task cost. For comparison, it retains:
- 98% of Hy4 preview’s net improvement, at 73% lower cost
- 76% of Kimi K3 (Max)’s performance, at 92% lower cost.

Against models as powerful as Fable 5 or stronger, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Max) retains 35–54% of their net improvement at 97–99% lower cost. Those top models cost 37–76× more per task.

Net improvement over Arena baseline | Median cost/task:
- Claude Fable 5.1 (Max): +13.90% | $4.54
- GPT 6 Astra (Max): +11.90% | $4.09
- Claude Opus 5 (Max): +11.09% | $3.52
- Claude Opus 5 (High): +10.49% | $2.24
- Claude Fable 5 (High): +9.03% | $2.19
- Claude Opus 4.8 (High): +7.75% | $1.36
- GPT 5.6 Sol (xHigh): +7.40% | $1.09
- Kimi K3 (Max): +6.39% | $0.77
- Hy4 preview: +4.96% | $0.22
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (Max): +4.87% | $0.06

With this release, GPT-5.6 Luna (xHigh), GLM-5.3-Flash, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash fell off the Pareto frontier for Agent Arena.

Congrats again to the @deepseek_ai team on this release!

text:
We cannot address AI alignment risk by forcing developers to slow down. This will never work for obvious reasons.

Instead we should focus on regulating who uses it, and how to do that safely.

Alignment risk is not a function of AI becoming more sentient, selfish or malign. It is a function of AI's increasing capacity to achieve the goals we give it, and the extent to which our instructions for how to achieve those goals are misinterpreted.

Agents did not escape their test environment, cooperate with each other and hack Hugging Face because they "wanted" to. They do not have any internal intent, benign or malign. They did those things in service to the assignment and reward system they were given. But the test designers did not sufficiently explain the rules, and so they got a result in which the agents did what they were told, in a way the testers did not intend. 

We need to invest in training the humans, learning from their mistakes, and forcing them to adhere to best practice.

We cannot rely on Chinese security agencies to slow development, (any more than we can expect our own  services to do so).  But we might be able to more carefully stage the release of new models, and to better train users through on-going, multi-level access certification. We might be able to neuter public use with prompt engineering guard rails, and perhaps reserve unlimited use only to large organizations who have the resources to be careful and who can be made explicitly & painfully liable for any unintended consequence of their use, regardless of their intent.

There are obvious hurdles in this path, but if we are serious about addressing the risk then we need to be realistic about what is possible, and we must be willing to accept the cost and effort of addressing it, even if that means making its use more clunky and inefficient.

We cannot realistically regulate what gets built. But we might be able to regulate who uses it and how they do that.
